alt-distal-inhibition-raises-somatic-thr: Distal dendritic inhibition cuts firing the same way perisomatic inhibition does, by raising the spike threshold rather than by suppressing dendritic spikes.
alt-perisomatic-and-distal-share-mechani: Perisomatic and distal inhibition work through one shared mechanism, so perisomatic inhibition also controls dendritic spiking.
alt-phase-modulation-requires-buildup: Phase-dependent control of dendritic spikes and spike timing needs many cycles of a rhythm to build up.
beta-bidirectional-dendritic-control: Beta-rhythm inhibition on distal dendrites both raises dendritic spiking in its troughs and suppresses it in its peaks.
beta-gates-distal-apical-inputs: Clustered apical inputs reach the soma when they arrive in the trough of a distal beta rhythm and are blocked at its peak.
beta-optimal-distal-dendritic-entrainmen: Across a sweep of rhythm frequencies, beta near 20 Hz locks distal dendritic Ca²⁺ and NMDA spikes to phase most strongly.
burst-effects-emerge-first-cycles: Phase-dependent control of dendritic spikes and spike timing appears within the first few cycles of a beta or gamma burst.
ca-spikes-couple-20ms-before-ap: Ca²⁺ spikes in apical tuft dendrites lead somatic action potentials by about 20 ms, most tightly in the most distal compartments.
distal-inhib-drops-firing-02hz: Doubling distal dendritic inhibition nearly silences the neuron by shutting down dendritic Ca²⁺ and NMDA spikes, not by raising spike threshold.
ei-lag-sensitivity-firing-rate: Changing the delay between excitation and inhibition barely moves the firing rate but changes which dendrites drive the spikes.
gamma-gates-proximal-basal-inputs: Gamma-rhythm inhibition near the soma gates clustered proximal and basal inputs by phase while leaving distal apical inputs largely alone.
gamma-optimal-perisomatic-ap-modulation: Across a sweep of rhythm frequencies, gamma modulates the somatic spike threshold most strongly when inhibition sits near the soma.
gamma-perisomatic-no-dendritic-spike-cha: Gamma rhythms near the soma shift the spike threshold by phase without changing how often dendritic spikes occur.
hypothesis-distinct-compartmental-roles: Perisomatic inhibition controls the soma's spike output, while distal dendritic inhibition controls dendritic spikes and their timing.
hypothesis-frequency-compartment-matchin: A rhythm controls a compartment best when its cycle matches the local spike timescale — gamma at the soma, beta at distal dendrites.
interprets-pv-gamma-sst-beta-association: Earlier work found that PV+ interneurons target the soma and accompany gamma, while SST+ interneurons target distal dendrites and beta.
l5-model-single-cell-scope: Every result comes from a compartmental model of one layer 5 pyramidal neuron, with no network or population effects simulated.
na-spikes-couple-2to3ms-before-ap: Na+ dendritic spikes in proximal compartments lead somatic action potentials by 2–3 ms, with coupling weakening farther from the soma.
naturalistic-drive-parameterization: Synaptic drive uses published experimental parameters and yields a typical in vivo firing rate, with no sensitivity analysis over those choices.
nmda-spikes-couple-25ms-before-ap: NMDA spikes lead somatic action potentials by about 25 ms, longer than Na+ spikes because their kinetics are slower.
perisomatic-inhib-drops-firing-07hz: Doubling perisomatic inhibition nearly silences the neuron by raising the spike threshold, while dendritic spikes carry on.
perisomatic-inhib-subtractive-divisive: Perisomatic inhibition lowers both the neuron's baseline firing and the slope of its input-output curve, compressing its dynamic range.
prediction-beta-optimal-distal: Distal inhibition should work best at beta, whose cycle matches the roughly 20–25 ms lead of dendritic spikes over somatic spikes.
prediction-distal-dendritic-spike-mechan: Doubling distal dendritic inhibition should cut firing by suppressing apical Ca²⁺ and NMDA spikes, leaving the spike threshold alone.
prediction-gamma-optimal-perisomatic: Perisomatic inhibition should work best at gamma, whose cycles match the 2–3 ms lead of proximal Na+ spikes over somatic spikes.
prediction-orthogonal-input-gating: Beta at the distal dendrites should gate apical inputs and gamma at the soma should gate basal inputs, each working independently.
prediction-perisomatic-input-output-shap: Perisomatic inhibition should both shift and flatten the somatic input-output curve rather than simply moving its operating point.
prediction-perisomatic-threshold-mechani: Doubling perisomatic inhibition should cut firing by raising the somatic spike threshold, leaving dendritic Ca²⁺ and NMDA spikes intact.
pv-gamma-sst-beta-correspondence: The model explains why PV+ cells pair with gamma and SST+ cells with beta: each rhythm is optimal where that cell type makes its synapses.
